articles.title: Department of War Publishes Second Release of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Files on WAR.GOV/UFO
articles.summary: The Department of War says it is publishing the second release of declassified and historical Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena files as part of the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters, or PURSUE. The release states that the collection remains housed on WAR.GOV/UFO and that additional files will be released on a rolling basis. Assistant to the Secretary of War for Public Affairs and Chief Pentagon Spokesman Sean Parnell is named as the source of the statement. The Department says WAR.GOV/UFO has received over 1 billion hits worldwide since its May 8, 2026 launch, which it frames as evidence of major public interest in the topic and in the Trump administration's transparency effort. The statement adds that the Department of War and agency partners are working on a third UAP file release, which will be announced in the near future.

articles.title: The Evidence Around UAPs Is Getting Harder to Ignore
articles.summary: png) 0:00 -10:15 Audio 3 Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence – such is the case on Non-Human Intelligence (NHI) and Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAPs). I have had no personal firsthand experience with either, but there is evidence mounting, and it has been significant enough that it has captured my attention. I want to share the way I think about this — not as a believer, not as a skeptic, but as someone who takes data seriously enough to know when too much is happening not to pay attention. On August 31, 2026, at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the UAP Science Advisory Council was informed that the United States government has a ‘**preparedness plan in place’** should the existence of nonhuman intelligence (NHI) be confirmed.

articles.title: Exeter UFO Festival 2026: Your complete guide to out-of-this-world speakers and events
articles.summary: Exeter UFO Festival 2026: Your complete guide to out-of-this-world speakers and events - The Exeter UFO Festival is a Labor Day weekend tradition celebrating the 1965 "Incident at Exeter. " - Hosted by the Exeter-Area Kiwanis Club, the two-day event features UFO expert talks, a parade, and an alien costume contest. - Activities include trolley rides to the 1965 sighting location and continuous showings of historical videos. - Proceeds from the festival and a special police patch sale support local children's charities and scholarships. If you’ve walked through downtown Exeter lately, you may have spotted neon‑green alien faces peering from storefronts and posters — a sure sign that the UFO Festival is about to return.

en.title: The Evidence Around UAPs Is Getting Harder to Ignore
en.summary: png) 0:00 -10:15 Audio 3 Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence – such is the case on Non-Human Intelligence (NHI) and Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAPs). I have had no personal firsthand experience with either, but there is evidence mounting, and it has been significant enough that it has captured my attention. I want to share the way I think about this — not as a believer, not as a skeptic, but as someone who takes data seriously enough to know when too much is happening not to pay attention.

de.title: Die Beweise für UAPs werden immer schwerer zu ignorieren
de.summary: png) 0:00 -10:15 Audio 3 Außergewöhnliche Ansprüche erfordern außergewöhnliche Beweise – dies ist der Fall bei nicht-menschlicher Intelligenz (nhi) und nicht identifizierten anomalen Phänomenen (UAPs). Ich habe keine persönlichen Erfahrungen aus erster Hand mit beiden gemacht, aber es gibt immer mehr Beweise, und es war signifikant genug, dass es meine Aufmerksamkeit erregt hat. Ich möchte die Art und Weise teilen, wie ich darüber denke — nicht als Gläubiger, nicht als Skeptiker, sondern als jemand, der Daten aufnimmt ernst genug, um zu wissen, wann zu viel passiert, um nicht darauf zu achten.

en.title: Exeter UFO Festival 2026: Your complete guide to out-of-this-world speakers and events
en.summary: Exeter UFO Festival 2026: Your complete guide to out-of-this-world speakers and events - The Exeter UFO Festival is a Labor Day weekend tradition celebrating the 1965 "Incident at Exeter. " - Hosted by the Exeter-Area Kiwanis Club, the two-day event features UFO expert talks, a parade, and an alien costume contest. - Activities include trolley rides to the 1965 sighting location and continuous showings of historical videos. - Proceeds from the festival and a special police patch sale support local children's charities and scholarships. If you’ve walked through downtown Exeter lately, you may have spotted neon‑green alien faces peering from storefronts and posters — a sure sign that the UFO Festival is about to return.
